title: Reserve Harmonics: Quick Tuner for Pool Autoscaling and Burst
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design a compact, single-pane 'Quick Tuner' for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, autoscale intent, and cost impact for burst windows. The goal is to give operators an approachable control to set autoscale thresholds, define short burst windows, and preview estimated per-hour cost and SLO risk — without leaving the pool list or drilling into full policy editor. This ticket covers explorational sketches, high-fidelity prototype, accessibility review, and a stakeholder design critique with Engineering and Product.
design_notes: UI pattern: single-row condensed card that expands to a micro-panel overlay. Keep primary controls (target throughput, min/max nodes, burst toggle) as compact inputs with contextual help hover states.

Visual affordance: harmonic waveform visualization that encodes historical load (lighter strokes) and proposed burst profile (accent color). The waveform is purely illustrative and must degrade to sparkline for accessibility and small screen sizes.
Cost preview: live calculation that shows a 1h/6h/24h estimate delta when burst is enabled. Use existing pricing table API; when unavailable show 'estimate unavailable' fallback.

Safety guard: SLO safety knob with three presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive). Setting influences autoscale cooldown and burst budget. Display inline risk badge (green/yellow/red) with short tooltip linking to console SLO docs.
Interaction model: changes persist to a draft state local to user until 'Apply' is pressed. Provide undo and 'Preview Rollout' to simulate effect across active routes.
Mobile/width breakpoints: panel must collapse to an icon with a numeric badge when width < 720px; full quick-tuner is tablet+ only.
Accessibility: ensure all controls reachable by keyboard; waveform has textual summary for screen readers; color choices meet AA contrast for badges and sliders.
Performance: avoid embedding heavy charts. Use canvas-based lightweight sparkline. Ensure panel open/close doesn't trigger heavy runtime flares or additional metric fetching beyond summary tiles.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype linked in attachments and navigable from pool list to micro-panel and back
Engineering review sign-off on data contract: historical 5m load, current capacity, pricing snapshot endpoint
Accessibility checklist completed and no critical violations
Design critique notes incorporated and follow-ups converted to sub-issues
Cost preview shows correct delta given mocked pricing in prototype and toggles update the sample calculation
review_feedback: PM (Lina Chen) requested clearer separation between temporary burst (one-off) and scheduled burst policy — we added a tiny pill that labels mode: 'One-time' vs 'Scheduled'.
Eng (Daniel Park) flagged potential backend cost API latency; recommended adding debounce and cached fallback mode — implemented in prototype via 'estimate pending' state.
SRE (Priya Nair) recommended exposing cooldown value prominently when aggressive safety preset is selected — added inline tooltip and default cooldown value display.
Design lead (Elliot Gomez) suggested reducing microcopy and relying more on iconography for repeated controls to avoid cognitive load; updated mock to use compact icons with accessible labels.
